newsitem.title: USA: Oil prices may trigger Mexico Brady oil warrants.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices may trigger Mexico Brady oil warrants.

text.p: Mexico may have to make its first warrant payments to holders of par bonds and discount bonds on December 31, Smith Barney said in a research report on Tuesday.
The payment is contingent on the average price of Mexico's exported oil remaining around the current $20.65 per barrel through the end of September, Smith Barney said.
The International Monetary Fund will make the final calculations as to the value of the warrants.

Smith Barney debt analyst James Barrineau estimated the total sum for the oil warrants, if they were indeed paid out, would come to $62 million. The loss in government revenue would be more than offset by the rise in oil prices, Barrineau said.
Smith Barney said the price of Mexico par and discount bonds should rise if the possibility of a warrant payment increases toward the end of September.

Mexican par and discount bonds contain Value Recovery Rights (VRRs), or oil warrants that entitle holders to receive a payment linked to the value of Mexico's oil export revenues on top of interest payments.
Smith Barney said that should the average oil price remain around $20.65 through September, Mexico may be required to make payments of about $550 per million par bonds and $850 per million discounts.
The investment bank estimated that this payment effectively raised the current coupon of pars by 0.25 percent and of discounts by 0.75 percent.

Mexican Brady prices should be helped by the high probability that the oil warrants will pay in the next year and the fact that warrants from a major Brady country have never been so close to in-the-money, Smith Barney said.

Under a complex formula, the additional payments required under the warrants depend on the average price per barrel of oil exported by Mexico, a reference oil price, current export volume and the amount of eligible debt that was exchanged for par and discount bonds, which was approximately $40 billion.
